- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to reflect mean reversion toward prior 10-day support.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out sentiment; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-day prices to anchor forecast, rather than pure trend extrapolation.
